def zip_equal(*iterables):
    """``zip`` the input *iterables* together, but raise ``UnequalIterablesError``
    if they have different lengths.

        >>> list(zip_equal([1, 2, 3], ['a', 'b', 'c']))
        [(1, 'a'), (2, 'b'), (3, 'c')]

        >>> list(zip_equal([1, 2, 3], ['a', 'b']))
        Traceback (most recent call last):
            ...
        more_itertools.more.UnequalIterablesError: zip_equal() argument 2 is shorter
          than argument 1

    This function is similar to :func:`zip`, except it will raise an error
    if the iterables have different lengths.
    """
    # Sentinel object to detect when one iterable is exhausted
    sentinel = object()
    
    # Convert all iterables to iterators
    iterators = [iter(it) for it in iterables]
    
    while True:
        items = []
        for i, it in enumerate(iterators):
            item = next(it, sentinel)
            if item is sentinel:
                # One iterable is exhausted; check if others also are
                # If any other iterable still has items, they're unequal
                for j, jt in enumerate(iterators):
                    if j != i:
                        next_item = next(jt, sentinel)
                        if next_item is not sentinel:
                            raise UnequalIterablesError(
                                f"zip_equal() argument {i + 1} is shorter "
                                f"than argument {j + 1}"
                            )
                # All remaining iterables are also exhausted, we're done
                return
            else:
                items.append(item)
        
        yield tuple(items)

def zip_equal(*iterables):
    """``zip`` the input *iterables* together, but raise ``UnequalIterablesError``
    if they have different lengths.

        >>> list(zip_equal([1, 2, 3], ['a', 'b', 'c']))
        [(1, 'a'), (2, 'b'), (3, 'c')]

        >>> list(zip_equal([1, 2, 3], ['a', 'b']))
        Traceback (most recent call last):
            ...
        more_itertools.more.UnequalIterablesError: zip_equal() argument 2 is shorter
          than argument 1

    This function is similar to :func:`zip`, except it will raise an error
    if the iterables have different lengths.
    """
    # Sentinel object to detect when one iterable is exhausted
    sentinel = object()
    
    # Convert all iterables to iterators
    iterators = [iter(it) for it in iterables]
    
    while True:
        items = []
        exhausted = False
        for i, it in enumerate(iterators):
            item = next(it, sentinel)
            if item is sentinel:
                if not exhausted:
                    exhausted = True
                    first_exhausted_index = i
                elif i != first_exhausted_index:
                    # One iterable was already exhausted, and this one too
                    raise UnequalIterablesError(
                        f"zip_equal() argument {i + 1} is shorter "
                        f"than argument {first_exhausted_index + 1}"
                    )
            else:
                if exhausted:
                    raise UnequalIterablesError(
                        f"zip_equal() argument {first_exhausted_index + 1} is shorter "
                        f"than argument {i + 1}"
                    )
                items.append(item)
        
        if exhausted:
            break
        
        yield tuple(items)
